subject: Re: PioneerHealth migration economics & shelf-credit structuring
messages:
From: Ava Jennings <ava.j@pioneerhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Becker <tbecker@fastcloud.io>
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pioneer migration economics — shelf credit ask

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking a look at this. We're running a competitive review internally and have a near-term window to kick off a migration if we can close economics and an implementation assurance package. Two asks from procurement: 1) can Redwood match the per-token economics we were offered by FastCloud for inference (they're offering an effective 25% unit discount on the models we're using), and 2) can you provide a one-time "shelf" credit to offset migration and egress risk (our finance team wants a buffer for potential performance delta during the first 60 days).

I've attached our current_contract_summary.pdf so you have the baseline. High level usage is ~60M generated tokens/month with spiky peak days at 150M. We prefer a mix of reserved and burstable capacity.

Procurement also asked for a HubSpot reference — HS-87654321 — and the SOC2 evidence for audit. Can you confirm what you can do on match and shelf credit and any constraints on timing?

Best,
Ava
Ava Jennings
Director, Product Integrations
PioneerHealth

Attachments: current_contract_summary.pdf (PDF)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Ava Jennings <ava.j@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pioneer migration economics — shelf credit ask

Ava — thanks for the clear framing and the contract summary. Looping in Marissa (AM), Connor (solutions), and Jordan (pricing) to run the numbers and propose a concrete structure.

Quick clarifying questions while they model:
- Can you confirm the % of traffic that is latency-sensitive (low latency SLA) vs batch?
- Do you have a preferred go-live window? Procurement mentioned "near-term" — are we looking at July start or later?

We'll produce an initial econ model (attachment) with two alternatives: (A) volume-based permanent discount that matches FastCloud's net effective unit price if you commit to a 12-month reserved baseline, and (B) a smaller per-unit discount + one-time shelf credit sized to cover 60 days of estimated variability (applied as an invoice credit). See initial_econ_model.xlsx attached.

I'll coordinate a short call tomorrow with your procurement if that works.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: initial_econ_model.xlsx (Excel)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Pioneer migration economics — shelf credit ask

Team — ran two pricing constructs against Ava's baseline (see attached option_matrix.csv):

Option 1 (Commit + Match):
- 12-month reserved baseline = 50M tokens/month (covers base usage)
- Effective unit price matched to FastCloud at volume tiers (requires 12-month commit)
- No shelf credit; instead we front-load an onboarding credit worth 10% of one month baseline on first invoice to offset ramping ops costs

Option 2 (Smaller Commit + Shelf Credit):
- 6-month reserved baseline = 40M tokens/month + burst capacity
- 10% per-token discount (not full match) + one-time shelf credit equal to estimated 60-day delta (~$45k) applied as invoice credit

Operational constraints / notes:
- Shelf credit must be defined in SOW as a non-recurring invoice-level credit — procurement prefers a guaranteed dollar bucket rather than conditional usage rebates.
- We need a migration window defined (2-week cutover preferred) to estimate egress/engineering hours.
- SOC2 evidence available; Connor, can you attach the audit pack to the HubSpot record?

I'll be on the call with Ava tomorrow, draft a clean comparison and proposed contract language for the SOW.

— Marissa
Attachment: option_matrix.csv
From: Ava Jennings <ava.j@pioneerhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Becker <tbecker@fastcloud.io>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 10:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pioneer migration economics — shelf credit ask

Thanks Marissa — that helps. A few quick clarifications from procurement and engineering:

- Procurement prefers Option 2 if the shelf credit is explicit and uncapped against implementation overruns (they want it structured as a $ credit applied within 90 days).
- Engineering wants a 4-week migration window (two weeks prep + two weeks cutover) given data validation and low-latency testing. That will increase uplift costs slightly.
- We're okay with a 6-month baseline commitment if Redwood will increase the shelf credit by 15% to account for the longer migration window.

Also, here's our HubSpot record HS-87654321 for reference. Tom from FastCloud is copied because procurement wants the exact offer compared side-by-side during the call.

Can you send a mutual action plan and a draft SOW language for the shelf credit (dollar amount, application timing, and carve-outs)? If we can get that by EOD we can schedule a procurement sign-off call for Wednesday.

Best,
Ava

Subject: Re: Pioneer migration economics — shelf credit ask

Ava / team — following up from the call (thanks all) with a recommended construct we can scope into the SOW:

Final recommended construct (per call):
- Baseline: 6-month reserved baseline at 40M tokens/month.
- Per-token pricing: 10% off list for the baseline tier; burst pricing at standard Redwood burst rates.
- Shelf credit: one-time $51,750 invoice credit (represents 75% of the 60-day delta estimate to account for the 4-week migration window) payable on first invoice after go-live. Credit is non-recurring, included in SOW, and expires 90 days post go-live if unused.
- Migration window: 4 weeks (2w prep + 2w cutover). Redwood will provide an onboarding engineer and a runbook; travel not included.
- Evidence & compliance: Connor will attach the SOC2 audit pack to HS-87654321 and share read-only Drive folder (link below).

Next steps:
1) Marissa will create a short SOW snippet and redline the pricing language (pricing_redline.docx attached).
2) I'll circulate MAP_Pioneer_2025.pdf (mutual action plan link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cPioneerMAP).
3) Procurement to confirm acceptance of the $51,750 shelf credit by Wednesday EOD.

If Pioneer confirms, we can get DocuSign ready and target a July 7 kickoff for the prep phase.

— Rachel
Attachments: MAP_Pioneer_2025.pdf, pricing_redline.docx
